title: "Shnayim Mikra..." - The Haftarah

chapters.title: Introduction to Haftarah and Shnayim Mikra
chapters.about: Introduction to the halakhot of Shnayim Mikra and the question of Haftarah.

chapters.title: Sources in Shulchan Aruch and Rama
chapters.about: Examining Shulchan Aruch's silence on Haftarah and Rama citing the Mordechai and Terumat HaDeshen.

chapters.about: Explaining the two approaches to Shnayim Mikra through Hagahot Maimoni and Hagahot Ashiri.

chapters.about: Concluding halakhic status and Rabbi Elyashiv's ruling for contemporary times.

claims: "He explores the different underlying rationales of Rabbeinu Simcha and Rabbeinu Hananel regarding the purpose of the weekly reading." - The transcript attributes these rationales to the Gemara/early authorities via Hagahot Maimonie/Ashiri, not as the teacher's own exploration of the weekly reading's purpose in general, but specifically in the context of the Shulchan Aruch's ruling on holiday readings.
summary: Rabbi Harari discusses whether there is a requirement or custom to read the Haftarah as part of Shnayim Mikra ve-Echad Targum, examining the sources in the Shulchan Aruch, Rama, and commentaries. He explores the different underlying rationales of Rabbeinu Simcha and Rabbeinu Hananel regarding the purpose of the weekly reading. He concludes that there is no strict halakhic obligation to read the Haftarah, though some have a custom to do so.
questions: Is there an obligation to read the Haftarah as part of Shnayim Mikra ve-Echad Targum?
What do the Shulchan Aruch and Rama say about reading the Haftarah?
How do the views of Rabbeinu Simcha and Rabbeinu Hananel differ regarding the purpose of Shnayim Mikra?
Does Magen Avraham require preparing the Haftarah for holidays and Shabbat?
What is the ruling of Rabbi Yosef Shalom Elyashiv regarding reading the Haftarah in modern times?
